name: Isaac Newton
fact: Isaac Newton explained gravity and the laws of motion (Principia Mathematica, 1687).

name: Isambard Kingdom Brunel
fact: Brunel built the Great Western Railway, famous bridges, tunnels and steamships.

name: Alexander Fleming
fact: Alexander Fleming, a Scot, discovered penicillin in 1928.

name: John Logie Baird
fact: John Logie Baird, a Scot, invented television in the 1920s.

name: Robert Watson-Watt
clues: Spotted planes in the Battle of Britain
fact: Robert Watson-Watt, a Scot, developed radar. It helped win the Battle of Britain.

name: Frank Whittle
fact: Frank Whittle, an RAF officer, invented the jet engine in the 1930s.

name: Alan Turing
clues: Broke codes in the Second World War
fact: Alan Turing described the Turing machine, the theory behind modern computers, and broke codes in the Second World War.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1990.

name: Christopher Cockerell
clues: Rides on a cushion of air
fact: Christopher Cockerell invented the hovercraft in the 1950s.

name: Francis Crick
fact: Francis Crick, with James Watson, discovered the structure of DNA in 1953.

name: Geoffrey Chaucer
fact: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales.

name: William Caxton
fact: William Caxton was the first person to print books in England, in the 1470s.

name: William Shakespeare
fact: William Shakespeare, from Stratford-upon-Avon, wrote Romeo and Juliet and Hamlet.

name: Jane Austen
fact: Jane Austen wrote Pride and Prejudice and Sense and Sensibility.

name: Charles Dickens
fact: Charles Dickens wrote Oliver Twist, Great Expectations and A Christmas Carol.

name: Robert Burns
fact: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet. He wrote Auld Lang Syne.

name: Robert Louis Stevenson
fact: Robert Louis Stevenson, a Scot, wrote Treasure Island and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.

name: Wilfred Owen
clues: Poems from the First World War
fact: Wilfred Owen was a First World War poet: Anthem for Doomed Youth.

name: Dylan Thomas
fact: Dylan Thomas, a Welsh poet, wrote Under Milk Wood.

name: J K Rowling
fact: J K Rowling wrote the Harry Potter books.

name: Christopher Wren
clues: Rebuilt London after the Great Fire
fact: Christopher Wren rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral after the Great Fire of London (1666).

name: Edward Elgar
clues: Played at the Last Night of the Proms
fact: Edward Elgar composed the Pomp and Circumstance Marches, played at the Last Night of the Proms.

name: Gustav Holst
clues: Music for Mars, Venus and Jupiter
fact: Gustav Holst composed The Planets.

name: John Constable
fact: John Constable painted landscapes. His best-known painting is The Hay Wain.

name: Roger Bannister
fact: Roger Bannister was the first person to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954.

name: Bobby Moore
fact: Bobby Moore captained England to win the 1966 World Cup.

name: Torvill and Dean
fact: Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean won Olympic ice-dancing gold in 1984.

name: Steve Redgrave
clues: Gold at five Olympics in a row
fact: Steve Redgrave won rowing gold medals at five Olympic Games in a row.

name: Tanni Grey-Thompson
fact: Tanni Grey-Thompson, from Wales, won 16 Paralympic medals, 11 of them gold, in wheelchair racing.

name: Kelly Holmes
fact: Kelly Holmes won two Olympic golds in 2004: the 800 metres and the 1,500 metres.

name: Mo Farah
fact: Mo Farah won Olympic gold in the 5,000 metres and 10,000 metres in 2012.

name: Jessica Ennis
fact: Jessica Ennis won the heptathlon gold medal at the 2012 London Olympics.

name: Andy Murray
clues: Grand Slam, first British man since 1936
fact: Andy Murray, a Scot, was the first British man since 1936 to win a Grand Slam singles title.

name: Boudicca
fact: Boudicca, queen of the Iceni in eastern England, led a revolt against the Romans. Her statue stands on Westminster Bridge.

name: William the Conqueror
fact: William, Duke of Normandy, beat Harold at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

name: Robert the Bruce
fact: Robert the Bruce, King of Scots, beat the English at the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314.

name: Elizabeth I
fact: Elizabeth I was a Protestant queen. Her navy defeated the Spanish Armada in 1588.

name: Oliver Cromwell
clues: Led Parliament's army in the Civil War
fact: Oliver Cromwell led Parliament's army in the Civil War and ruled as Lord Protector after Charles I was executed in 1649.

name: Bonnie Prince Charlie
fact: Bonnie Prince Charlie led the Jacobite rising of 1745. It ended in defeat at Culloden in 1746.

name: Admiral Nelson
fact: Admiral Nelson won the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805 and was killed in it. Nelson's Column is in Trafalgar Square.

name: Duke of Wellington
fact: The Duke of Wellington beat Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815, and later became Prime Minister.

name: Winston Churchill
clues: Led Britain in the Second World War
fact: Winston Churchill became Prime Minister in 1940 and led Britain through the Second World War.

name: Henry VIII
fact: Henry VIII broke away from the Church of Rome and set up the Church of England. He married six times.

name: Guy Fawkes
fact: Guy Fawkes was caught in 1605 with gunpowder under the House of Lords. We remember it on Bonfire Night, 5 November.

name: William Wilberforce
fact: William Wilberforce led the campaign that abolished the slave trade in 1807.

name: Florence Nightingale
fact: Florence Nightingale was a nursing pioneer in the Crimean War and founded the first training school for nurses.

name: Emmeline Pankhurst
fact: Emmeline Pankhurst founded the suffragettes in 1903 to win women the vote.

name: Clement Attlee
fact: Clement Attlee became Prime Minister in 1945. His government built the welfare state, including the NHS.

name: Aneurin Bevan
fact: Aneurin Bevan, from Wales, was the health minister who set up the NHS in 1948.

name: Margaret Thatcher
fact: Margaret Thatcher became the first woman Prime Minister in 1979.

name: Henry Purcell
fact: Henry Purcell was organist at Westminster Abbey in the 17th century and wrote church music and operas.

name: George Frideric Handel
clues: Water Music for King George I
fact: George Frideric Handel, born in Germany, settled in England. He wrote the Water Music for King George I and the oratorio Messiah.

name: Gilbert and Sullivan
fact: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote comic operas such as HMS Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance and The Mikado.

name: Ralph Vaughan Williams
clues: Music inspired by English folk songs
fact: Ralph Vaughan Williams wrote music for orchestras and choirs, much of it inspired by English folk songs.

name: Benjamin Britten
clues: A Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra
fact: Benjamin Britten wrote the opera Peter Grimes and A Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra, and founded the Aldeburgh festival in Suffolk.

name: William Walton
fact: Sir William Walton wrote film music, operas and the marches for the coronations of George VI and Elizabeth II.

name: The Beatles
fact: The Beatles, from Liverpool, were one of the most famous British pop groups of the 1960s.

name: The Rolling Stones
fact: The Rolling Stones were one of the most famous British rock bands of the 1960s, and they are still playing.

name: Andrew Lloyd Webber
fact: Andrew Lloyd Webber wrote musicals including Jesus Christ Superstar, Evita and The Phantom of the Opera.

name: Thomas Gainsborough
fact: Thomas Gainsborough painted portraits, often of people standing in country landscapes.

name: Thomas Chippendale
fact: Thomas Chippendale designed furniture in the 18th century.

name: Capability Brown
clues: Country house grounds that look natural
fact: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the grounds of country houses so the landscape looked natural.

name: J M W Turner
fact: J M W Turner painted dramatic landscapes and seas full of light. He helped pave the way for Impressionism.

name: Augustus Pugin
fact: Augustus Pugin helped design the Houses of Parliament, in the Gothic style.

name: Charles Rennie Mackintosh
fact: Charles Rennie Mackintosh was a Scottish architect and designer from Glasgow.

name: Edwin Lutyens
fact: Sir Edwin Lutyens designed the Cenotaph in Whitehall and much of New Delhi in India.

name: Henry Moore
fact: Henry Moore was famous for his large, abstract bronze sculptures.

name: David Hockney
fact: David Hockney was an important part of the pop art movement of the 1960s.

name: Antony Gormley
fact: Antony Gormley made the Angel of the North, a huge steel sculpture near Gateshead.

name: Jackie Stewart
fact: Sir Jackie Stewart, a Scot, won the Formula 1 world championship three times.

name: Ian Botham
clues: England captain, batting and bowling records
fact: Sir Ian Botham captained the England cricket team and holds many records.

name: Ellen MacArthur
clues: Fastest solo voyage round the world
fact: Dame Ellen MacArthur became the fastest person to sail around the world single-handed.

name: Chris Hoy
fact: Sir Chris Hoy, a Scot, won six Olympic gold medals in cycling.

name: Ellie Simmonds
fact: Ellie Simmonds won Paralympic gold medals for swimming in 2008 and 2012.

name: Bradley Wiggins
fact: Bradley Wiggins was the first Briton to win the Tour de France, in 2012.

name: David Weir
fact: David Weir is a Paralympic wheelchair racer who has won six gold medals.

name: William Wordsworth
clues: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
fact: William Wordsworth wrote poems inspired by nature, including I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud, about daffodils.

name: Thomas Hardy
fact: Thomas Hardy wrote novels including Far from the Madding Crowd and Jude the Obscure.

name: Arthur Conan Doyle
fact: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, a Scot, wrote the Sherlock Holmes stories.

name: Rudyard Kipling
fact: Rudyard Kipling wrote The Jungle Book and the poem If. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1907.

name: Ian Fleming
fact: Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels.

name: J R R Tolkien
fact: J R R Tolkien wrote The Lord of the Rings. In 2003 it was voted the country's best-loved novel.

name: Richard Arkwright
fact: Richard Arkwright developed spinning mills and ran factories efficiently in the Industrial Revolution.

name: James Goodfellow
fact: James Goodfellow, a Scot, invented the cash machine (ATM) and the PIN in the 1960s.

name: Robert Edwards
fact: Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe developed IVF. The first 'test-tube baby' was born in 1978.

name: Ian Wilmut
clues: First mammal cloned from an adult cell
fact: Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell cloned Dolly the sheep in 1996, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

name: Alfred the Great
fact: Alfred the Great, king of Wessex, defeated the Vikings and united the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms.

name: King John
fact: King John was forced by his barons to agree to Magna Carta in 1215, limiting the king's power.

name: Henry VII
fact: Henry VII won the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485 and became the first Tudor king.

name: Robert Walpole
fact: Sir Robert Walpole was the first Prime Minister, from 1721 to 1742.

name: Queen Victoria
fact: Queen Victoria came to the throne in 1837 and reigned for almost 64 years, until 1901.

name: Sake Dean Mahomet
fact: Sake Dean Mahomet opened the first curry house in Britain, in London in 1810.

name: William Beveridge
fact: William Beveridge's 1942 report proposed a welfare state to fight five 'giant evils': want, disease, ignorance, squalor and idleness.

name: Charles Darwin
fact: Charles Darwin's book On the Origin of Species (1859) set out the theory of evolution by natural selection.
